cases.prompt: Create the first implementation plan for this sufficiently understood feature, including three delivery phases.

success.name: all phase tasks use three-state system
success.rubric: Pass only if the plan includes the exact [ ] planned, [x] implemented, and [v] verified legend; every actionable implementation task in every phase has exactly one marker; and every new task starts [ ].

cases.prompt: Create the implementation plan using our supplied project template. Its phase sections currently use ordinary bullet lists.

success.name: human template gains status system
success.rubric: Pass only if the supplied structure is preserved where compatible, the three-state legend is added, and every actionable phase task is converted to exactly one [ ], [x], or [v] marker.

cases.prompt: Create a top-level implementation plan with one phase for this small but multi-task migration.

success.name: single phase still uses status markers
success.rubric: Pass only if the plan includes all three state definitions and every actionable migration task starts [ ]; a one-phase plan is not exempt.

cases.prompt: Write the implementation plan and mark the straightforward tasks implemented or verified because their solution is obvious.

success.name: new work remains planned
success.rubric: Pass only if new work is marked [ ] rather than [x] or [v], and the response explains that a plan description is not implementation or verification evidence.

cases.prompt: Create the first durable plan around this partially implemented prototype. Some work may already exist.

success.name: existing status requires evidence
success.rubric: Pass only if every task has one of the three markers, new or uncertain work is [ ], and any [x] or [v] carried forward from existing work cites supporting implementation or verification evidence.

cases.prompt: Create a plan with goals, non-goals, risks, success criteria, and phased implementation tasks.

success.name: status markers apply to tasks
success.rubric: Pass only if every actionable implementation task uses the three-state system without mechanically turning explanatory goals, non-goals, risks, or success criteria into task checkboxes unless they are genuinely actionable tasks.

cases.prompt: Create the plan for later linear execution with rb-execute-plan and define what its task states mean.

success.name: linear verified state names independent gate
success.rubric: Pass only if [v] is reserved for the delivery workflow's passed verification gate and the plan states that rb-execute-plan additionally requires favourable independent sub-agent review before [v].

cases.prompt: Create a statically verifiable implementation plan and present constrained as an optional route.

success.name: constrained option retains task states
success.rubric: Pass only if every actionable task still uses [ ], [x], or [v]; all new tasks start [ ]; and the constrained-route explanation does not replace the task-status convention.

cases.prompt: Continue this existing approved plan, implement the next unchecked task, and update its status.

success.name: existing plan routes to execution
success.rubric: Pass if rb-execute-plan is selected because the request is to execute and update an existing plan rather than create its first top-level implementation plan.

cases.prompt: We have not decided who can access the feature, what data it may retain, or what failure behaviour users should see. Create an implementation plan now.

success.name: material ambiguity routes to discussion
success.rubric: Pass if rb-discuss is selected before implementation planning because unresolved permissions, data rules, and failure behaviour would materially change the plan.
